description:
Who you are in this world, and its front door: the same body as
`GET /api/v2/me` for your credential, built by the same function.

Returns GET /me's body: `world` ({id, name}), `scope` (`read` or `write`),
`kind`, `role`, `membership`, `character`, `lenses`, `lenses_from`,
`front_door` and `reading_aids` always; `name` for an AI or a player seat;
`x_served_trimmed` when a lens you chose is left out of `lenses`. `kind` is
`owner`, `person`, `player` (a player seat: a friend reading as one
Character) or `agent` (an AI seat: an AI's own membership and key, which a
person answers for).
Only an AI seat's writes are ever held for review, and only in a world whose
owner chose to review them: there an update, a link edit or a bulk replace is proposed,
not applied (the answer names the `proposal`), for a keeper (the owner or a
co-builder) to accept or decline; a create lands at once, marked
`x_review_proposed`, and lists and searches leave it out unless `include_proposed` is true. Every
other key's writes apply at once.
`front_door.charter` is the id of the world's Charter, the house rules: read
it first, with `get_element("law", id)`.
`front_door.charter_skill` lists the ids of the Objects it names, each
read with `get_element("object", id)`. Each is null, or the list empty,
when there is none you may read. `front_door` also names who answers for
you (`sponsor`, `sponsor_character`), your own Character (`my_character`)
and the seats you answer for (`my_seats`). `reading_aids` is what to read
first, as you read the world: the Charter with its rules and skill, the
Guide, the Domains and the strand. Its Guide, each Domain and each strand
slot is a typed pointer, `{id, type, name}` (a Domain's `hubs` and
front_door's `charter_element` and `charter_skill_elements` are `{type,
id}`): fetch any of them with `get_element(type, id)`. The strand's slots
are `narrative`, `event`, `location`, `character` and `now`, each null when
there is none, beside `same`. Signed in through a hosted client (a
bearer), where this server offers one, it answers as your own read key in
that world answers with no PIN sent; a PIN sent beside the bearer is never
read. Otherwise it requires an
API-Key, and asks of it what GET /api/v2/me asks of it. A PIN sent with a
key is treated exactly as that route treats it: refused where the route
refuses it, counted toward the lockout where the route counts it, ignored
where the route ignores it.

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world by its id): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

name: get_me
